prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1062; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a low-speed head-on collision. Insured vehicle and third-party vehicle both reported minor front-end damage. Claimant reports neck strain and is represented by counsel. Requested all communications be routed through the attorney's office. Photos of both vehicles requested from the insured and tow status confirmed.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant's attorney's office to acknowledge representation and confirm the claim is open. Requested the police report, medical authorization form, and any treatment records available at this stage. Advised that the liability determination is pending review of the scene documentation and statements from both drivers.

Entry 3: Reviewed photos and estimate from the body shop for the insured vehicle. Damage appears consistent with the reported impact speed and direction. Third-party vehicle inspection scheduled. Reserve set for property damage and an initial amount for bodily injury pending receipt of medical records.

Entry 4: Received a partial medical summary from claimant's attorney showing an evaluation for neck strain, follow-up physical therapy recommended, and no imaging findings of fracture. Requested complete records and billing from all treating providers. Noted that the claimant has not yet returned to full work duties according to counsel.

Entry 5: Completed recorded statements review and preliminary liability assessment. Coverage confirmed under the insured's policy. Forwarded the file to the bodily injury unit for evaluation of the claim with counsel. Diary set to follow up with the attorney's office for updated treatment status and outstanding records.
